lens: The intersection of ACE inhibitors and aging lacks mechanistic evidence in humans; existing literature focuses on cardiovascular outcomes in heart failure or hypertension cohorts, not on direct aging biomarkers like telomere length, senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) markers, or proteostasis regulators in older adults.
known_to_ignore: ACE inhibitors lower blood pressure in elderly hypertensives
ACE inhibitors reduce mortality in heart failure patients
tensions: Blood pressure targets differ by age (<60 vs ≥60 years) in guidelines, but no ACE inhibitor-specific aging outcome studies exist to justify these thresholds
Heart failure trials (e.g., aliskiren/enalapril in paper 10.1093/eurjhf/hfs033) show safety concerns in elderly with comorbidities (e.g., stroke risk), yet aging-specific biomarker data are absent
gaps: No human studies on ACE inhibitor effects on cellular senescence markers in adults >70 years
No dose-response data for ACE inhibitors (e.g., enalapril 10mg vs 20mg) on age-related outcomes like sarcopenia or cognitive decline
No comparative data between ACE inhibitors and other antihypertensives on aging hallmarks in hypertensive cohorts
reviewer_objections: Without primary data on aging biomarkers, any thesis would be speculative
The evidence pool lacks even basic epidemiological data linking ACE inhibitor use to aging phenotypes in humans
next_extractions: Search for ACE inhibitor studies measuring SASP factors (IL-6, TNF-α) in older cohorts
Extract data on ACE inhibitor use and telomere length from existing hypertension trials
Investigate ACE inhibitor effects on mTOR or autophagy markers in aged animal models with human translation potential
